newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to resume PGM exports in June - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Russia to resume PGM exports in June - Tass.

text.p: Russia will resume exports of platinum group metals in June, Itar-Tass news agency quoted Yuri Kotlyar, first deputy chief executive Norilsk Nickel, a major PGM producer, as saying on Tuesday.

Kotlyar, the former acting head of the disbanded Roskomdragmet state committee for precious metals and stones, was quoted as saying bureaucractic delays connected to the reorganisation of government bodies dealing with precious metals were to blame for the delays in Russian PGM exports.
Kotlyar cited the liquidation of Roskomdragmet last year and the dissolution of the Industry Ministry in a recent government reshuffle as partly behind Russia's delays in resuming PGM exports.
Tass said the changes had delayed procedures used for establishing export quotas and awarding export licences, but it gave no further details.

Russia accounts for about 60 percent of the world's palladium supply and around 20 percent of platinum deliveries, with Norilsk Nickel accounting for most of Russian production. Japan is the world's biggest consumer of the white metals, which have shot to highs over worries about the Russian delays.
Russia, whose Almazjuvelirexport agency has returned from contract talks in Tokyo, has not said exactly when it will resume supplies or in what volumes.
